task.text:
[0] EF-1a transgenic flied lived longer than control transgenic flies, although none of them lived longer than wild-type flies. Although there is a clear difference in mean lifespan between the EF-1a transgenic flies and the control transgenic flies, EF-1a transgenic flies do not express more EF-1a protein or mRNA than control flies kept at the same experimental conditions. Authors conclude that the experimental flies examined here do not live longer because of overexpressing the EF-1a gene.

[1] EF-1a transgenic flied lived longer than control transgenic flies, although none of them lived longer than wild-type flies. Although there is a clear difference in mean lifespan between the EF-1a transgenic flies and the control transgenic flies, EF-1a transgenic flies do not express more EF-1a protein or mRNA than control flies kept at the same experimental conditions. Authors conclude that the experimental flies examined here do not live longer because of overexpressing the EF-1a gene.

[2] The age was counted from the first day of adulthood. 100 µg/ml of ampicillin, 20 µg/ml of tetracycline, and 1 mM IPTG were added to the culture media.

[3] Knockout of fibulin-3 (EFEMP1) in mice provoked an early-onset of aging phenotype. EFEMP1 -/- mice of C57BL/6 but not BALB/c background developed multiple hernias.

[4] 0.05–0.1 mg/mL of FUDR was added to the culture media. Age was counted from the first day of adulthood.

[5] Strikingly, most of the transgenic mice died at 7-9 months without any apparent causes of death or visible changes observed by autopsy. The average lifespan of eIF-5A2 mice is 8 months. % of lifespan decrease cannot be calculated from the shown data.

[6] EPS8 knockout mice showed calorie-restricted phenotype, mediated by a morphogenetic defect in intestine microvilli, and increased lifespan, compared to control.

[7] Muscle-specific knockdown of eps-8 after development extends lifespan C. elegans. 100 μg ml−1 5-fluoro-2′deoxyuridine (FUdR) was added to prevent the development of progeny.

[8] Neuronal-specific knockdown of eps-8 after development extends lifespan C. elegans. 100 μg ml−1 5-fluoro-2′deoxyuridine (FUdR) was added to prevent the development of progeny.

[9] The ubiquitination of EPS-8 was blocked by generating lysine (K) to arginine (R) mutants. Ubiquitin-less mutations did not result in loss of EPS-8 function, as EPS-8(K524R/K583R/K621R) mutants did not exhibit embryonic lethality or developmental arrest. However, EPS-8(K524R/K583R/K621R) worms had upregulated EPS-8 protein levels at young adult stages, resulting in a short-lived phenotype. 100 μg ml−1 5-fluoro-2′deoxyuridine (FUdR) was added to prevent the development of progeny.

Each numbered passage describes one lifespan experiment. For each, report three things using ONLY that passage:
  organism: the model organism studied, one lowercase word
  direction: exactly one of 'increases lifespan', 'decreases lifespan', or 'no change'
  method: how the gene was altered, e.g. gene knockout, overexpression, mutation, knockdown

Output one block per passage, in order, formatted exactly:
[0]
organism: ...
direction: ...
method: ...

Nothing else. If a passage does not state something, write 'unstated'.
